hunks.baseline: Most people you meet just pass through your life by chance, then gradually fade from your memory. Their names. Their faces.
hunks.sol: Most pass through your life by chance, then gradually fade from your memory. Their names. Their faces.

hunks.baseline: But there are exceptions to everything.
hunks.sol: But there are exceptions.

hunks.baseline: Like the guy sprinting toward me at full speed, right as I set foot on the landing.
hunks.sol: Like the guy sprinting toward me just as I set foot on the landing.

hunks.baseline: Was this guy a coincidence in my life, or a connection?
hunks.sol: Was this guy a chance encounter, or a connection that would stick?

hunks.baseline: Though right now, he looked about as happy as a dog who’d found the owner it thought it had lost.
hunks.sol: Right now, though, he looked like a dog reunited with an owner it thought it had lost.

hunks.baseline: The young man, who’d been panting away as if to prove just how poor his stamina was, heard my mutter and stared at me in shock.
hunks.sol: The young man had been panting away as if to prove just how poor his stamina was. At my mutter, he stared at me in shock.

hunks.baseline: But instead of saying that out loud, I answered shamelessly.
hunks.sol: I answered shamelessly anyway.

hunks.baseline: I’d shown him some goodwill and found out his name. A perfect bit of banter had me feeling rather pleased with myself—until the young man looked back and forth between Hyuk Mujin and me with a completely flat expression.
hunks.sol: I’d shown him some goodwill and found out his name. I was feeling rather pleased with our perfect teamwork—until the young man looked back and forth between Hyuk Mujin and me with a flat expression.

hunks.baseline: After a brief silence, I carefully opened my mouth.
hunks.sol: After a brief silence, I spoke carefully.

hunks.baseline: At Ju Wongong’s deeply wounded cry, everyone around us turned to look at me. Their voices were hushed, of course.
hunks.sol: At Ju Wongong’s deeply wounded cry, everyone around us turned to look at me. I could hear their hushed voices, too.

hunks.baseline: I sentenced Hyuk Mujin to death with a glare, then spoke as calmly as I could.
hunks.sol: I sentenced Hyuk Mujin to death with a glare, then spoke as calmly as I could, keeping a close eye on Ju Hwaran. She’d clapped a hand over her mouth.

hunks.baseline: At the coachman’s vigorous crack of the whip, the splendid carriage drawn by six fine horses raced down the smooth highway.
hunks.sol: The coachman cracked his whip, and the splendid carriage drawn by six fine horses raced down the smooth highway.

hunks.baseline: *Clip-clop, clip-clop, clip-clop!*
hunks.sol: *Thud-thud-thud-thud!*

hunks.baseline: With dozens of mounted soldiers escorting the enormous carriage, and a golden flag marking it as belonging to the imperial family, the crowd parted like the Red Sea.
hunks.sol: Dozens of mounted soldiers escorted the enormous carriage, and the golden flag marked it as belonging to the imperial family. The road parted before us like the Red Sea.

hunks.baseline: Commoners along the road, young and old, hurriedly dropped to the ground. Even the fat, powerful official who’d been lounging in a sedan chair carried by four sturdy men climbed down with a wobble.
hunks.sol: Commoners along the road, young and old, hurriedly dropped to the ground. Even the fat, powerful official who’d been lording it over everyone from a sedan chair carried by four men climbed down with a wobble.

hunks.baseline: I peered out through the lattice window and looked at Ju Wongong.
hunks.sol: I peered out through the lattice window, then looked at Ju Wongong.

hunks.baseline: It had been over four months by Murim’s reckoning since I last saw him. He seemed more full of life than before.
hunks.sol: I hadn’t seen him in over four months by Murim’s reckoning. He looked even more full of life than before.

hunks.baseline: Well, of course he was doing better. The last time I saw him, he’d looked more like a drowned corpse than a person.
hunks.sol: Well, of course he did. The last time I saw him, he’d looked more like a drowned corpse than a person.

hunks.baseline: It seemed his face wasn’t the only thing that had changed while we were apart. Had he learned to read minds? Ju Wongong spoke out of nowhere, stroking his neatly trimmed beard.
hunks.sol: Apparently his face wasn’t the only thing that had changed. Had he learned to read minds? Ju Wongong spoke out of nowhere, stroking his neatly trimmed beard.

hunks.baseline: “And yet you launched a pleasure boat and had a great time.”
hunks.sol: “And yet you were out having a great time on a pleasure boat.”

hunks.baseline: Ju Wongong faltered at my words, then changed his tune.
hunks.sol: Ju Wongong faltered, then changed his tune.

hunks.baseline: After spending half an hour explaining the whole “time our captain went from the Night King to a blushing innocent, then became a Supreme Peak-level homosexual” incident, I gazed off to one side with a deliberately mournful look and continued.
hunks.sol: After spending half an hour explaining the whole “That Time Our Captain Denied Going from the Night King to a Blushing Innocent and Becoming a Supreme Peak-Level Lover of Men” business, I gazed mournfully off to one side and continued.

hunks.baseline: In one corner of the carriage, still racing without pause, a bloody mess—no, Hyuk Mujin—was sprawled against the luxurious interior.
hunks.sol: In one corner of the carriage, still racing along without pause, a bloody mess—no, Hyuk Mujin—was sprawled against the luxurious interior.

hunks.baseline: “This won’t do. I’m really hurt. Get out of the carriage. I’m going back to my hometown right now.”
hunks.sol: “That’s it. I’m really hurt. Get out of the carriage. I’m going straight back to my hometown.”

hunks.baseline: “P-Prince Shangshan! Diapers!”
hunks.sol: “P-Prince Shangshan! Poopy diapers!”

hunks.baseline: He was a distant imperial relative, with no real claim to the throne.

He lacked the nerve, ability, and backing to make such a claim, and his only real talent was drinking, chasing women, and gambling. There couldn’t have been a more suitable person to fill an empty seat for a while.

hunks.sol: His appointment might only be temporary, but his personal incompetence didn’t diminish the authority of the City Lord of Sichuan Province.
